chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not swear oaths except by God. And whoever swears by God, let him be truthful. And whoever is sworn to by God, let him be pleased. And whoever is sworn to by God but is not pleased — he is not of God, Mighty and Majestic.'

key_terms.تَحْلِفُوا: swearing oaths (yameen) — a formal commitment invoking God's name as witness
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — divine epithet emphasizing God's transcendence and power
key_terms.فَلْيَرْضَ: let him be pleased — moral duty to accept an oath sworn by God
key_terms.فَلْيَصْدُقْ: let him be truthful — obligation of honesty when invoking God's name

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about swearing oaths by God in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a ruling from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), as narrated through the chain ending with Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin). The Prophet forbids swearing oaths by anything other than God, and establishes three duties: the one who swears must be truthful, the one for whom an oath is sworn must accept it, and failure to accept God's name as sufficient cause for satisfaction places one outside divine fellowship. This reflects the Islamic prohibition on swearing by created things (polytheistic oaths) and emphasizes the sanctity of God's name in contractual and social obligations.
